signal: Matching brackets, nested structure, undo operations, or evaluating an expression
why: The most recent unmatched item is always the next one to resolve, which is exactly last-in-first-out.

signal: For each element find the nearest greater or smaller element, a span, or the largest rectangle in a histogram
why: Keep indices on a stack ordered by value; each index is pushed once and popped once, so all answers come out in linear time.

signal: Maximum or minimum of every window of size k, or a DP that takes the best of the last k states
why: Drop candidates that can never be the maximum again; the front of the deque is always the current window maximum.

signal: Fewest moves in a grid or unweighted graph, or a process that spreads outward one layer at a time
why: A queue visits nodes in order of distance, so the first time you reach a node is via a shortest path.

signal: Count pairs or subarrays with a target sum, equal values, or equal prefix state
technique: Hash map of counts (often with prefix sums)
why: Instead of scanning all earlier positions, look up in O(1) how many earlier states complete the condition.
constraints: n up to 2*10^5; beware adversarial keys with unordered_map

signal: Group items that are 'the same up to some transformation' (anagrams, rotations, equivalent forms)
technique: Canonical form as a hash key
why: Map every item to a canonical signature (sorted letters, normalised tuple); equal signatures mean equivalent items.

signal: Compare many substrings for equality, or find repeated substrings, without an expensive character-by-character check
why: Prefix hashes let you compute the hash of any substring in O(1); equal hashes mean equal strings with high probability.
constraints: use a random base and a large modulus to resist anti-hash tests

signal: Order jobs or items to minimise a total (weighted completion time, lateness) where swapping two neighbours changes only their own contribution
technique: Sort by a comparator proved with an exchange argument
why: If any out-of-order adjacent pair can be swapped without making things worse, sorting by that key is optimal.

signal: Pick the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals, or the fewest points that hit every interval
technique: Sort by right end, take greedily
why: Choosing the interval that finishes earliest leaves the most room for the rest.

signal: Jobs with deadlines and profits, or 'always process the cheapest/best currently available item' as time advances
why: A heap exposes the best available candidate in O(log n) while newly available items keep arriving.

signal: A greedy choice looks natural but you cannot prove it (coin systems, knapsack-like capacity limits)
technique: Stress-test the greedy, then switch to DP
why: A single counterexample kills a greedy; brute force on small inputs finds it quickly and tells you to use dynamic programming instead.
